name: North Korea
genZNote: North Korea runs on its own calendar (Year 1 = 1912, Kim Il Sung's birth) and its own time zone experiments — it's less a country you visit for vacation and more a case study every geopolitics exam loves to ask about.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Geography
bullets: Occupies the northern half of the Korean Peninsula in East Asia, bordered by South Korea across the DMZ, and by China and a short stretch of Russia to the north.
Mostly mountainous and forested terrain, with major population centres and industry concentrated in western coastal plains around the capital, Pyongyang.
Temperate climate with cold, dry winters influenced by Siberian air masses.

sections.heading: 🗣️ People & Culture
bullets: Korean is the official language; culture and public life are heavily shaped by the state ideology of Juche (self-reliance) and the cult of personality around the ruling Kim family.
Traditional Korean customs, cuisine, and festivals are practiced, but public cultural expression is tightly controlled and centrally organised by the state.
Mass performances, state media, and monuments to the Kim family are prominent features of public life.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Government & Society
bullets: A single-party state under the Workers' Party of Korea, with power concentrated in the Kim family since the country's founding in 1948.
Officially named the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK); described by most international observers as one of the world's most closed and tightly controlled societies.
The economy and society are organised around a centrally planned, state-directed model with the military given priority ('Songun', military-first policy).

sections.heading: 🌐 Global Relations
bullets: Technically still at war with South Korea, as the 1953 Korean War ended in an armistice, not a peace treaty.
Subject to extensive United Nations Security Council sanctions over its nuclear weapons and ballistic missile programmes.
China is by far North Korea's most significant diplomatic and economic partner; Russia ties have also grown in recent years.

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 Relations with India
bullets: India maintains formal diplomatic relations with North Korea, but the relationship is limited in scope compared to India's ties with South Korea.
India has historically supported denuclearisation of the Korean Peninsula and complies with UN sanctions restricting trade and technology transfers with North Korea.
There is little significant trade or cultural exchange between the two countries at present.

sections.heading: 📦 Trade & Economy
bullets: A centrally planned economy, heavily sanctioned internationally, with limited transparency about its actual economic performance.
China is the overwhelming majority trade partner, given the extent of international sanctions on North Korea.
Known international revenue sources reportedly include mineral exports, overseas labour, and, according to international investigators, cyber-enabled financial theft.

sections.heading: ⭐ What It's Known For
bullets: Being one of the world's most isolated and tightly state-controlled countries.
An active nuclear weapons and ballistic missile programme, a major focus of international diplomacy and sanctions.
The Juche ideology of self-reliance and the multi-generational Kim family leadership.
The Korean Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) separating it from South Korea.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: North Korea (DPRK) is a single-party, centrally planned East Asian state under Kim family leadership, internationally sanctioned over its nuclear programme.
keyFacts: Capital: Pyongyang. Currency: North Korean Won.
Single-party state under the Workers' Party of Korea; ruled by the Kim family since 1948.
Technically still at war with South Korea (1953 armistice, no peace treaty).
Subject to extensive UN sanctions over nuclear/missile programmes.
commonConfusion: North Korea's official name is the Democratic People's Republic of Korea — it is not a liberal democracy despite the name.

highYieldFacts: North Korea: single-party state, capital Pyongyang, Juche ideology, Kim family rule since 1948.
Still technically at war with South Korea; 1953 agreement was an armistice.
Heavily sanctioned by the UNSC over nuclear weapons and missile tests.
commonTraps: Assuming 'Democratic' in its official name reflects its actual system of government.
Confusing North Korea's isolation with having no international relations at all — China remains a major partner.
mustRemember: North Korea: isolated, sanctioned, single-party nuclear state; China is its key partner; still formally at war with South Korea.
